title: Coordinate cross-team acceptance matrix for Private VPC upgrade toggle
creator: Luca Martinez
description: PRD: Add a user-facing toggle in the Redwood Console to enable the Private VPC upgrade path (v2 networking + optional KMS-based envelope encryption). This ticket coordinates cross-team acceptance criteria and sign-offs required before the toggle ships: engineering readiness for migration hooks and rollout flags; design acceptance for console UX, error states, and migration prompts; legal/compliance confirmation for data residency and export control language. Scope clarifications added after initial PRD: KMS integration will be optional for first wave; migration rollback path must be automated; customers with Reserved Dedicated instances are out of scope for this rollout. Goal: produce a single acceptance matrix and checklist that individual teams can sign off against to unblock release-2026.03.
acceptance_criteria: Engineering provides a migration-runbook and end-to-end test plan; test plan includes automated rollback validation and smoke tests for latency and KV-cache correctness
Design approves final console mockups and a microcopy package for the toggle, migration modal, and failure states
Legal confirms updated customer-facing Terms addendum and data residency wording; written approval attached
Security review (KMS path) completed with remediation items triaged and assigned
A signed cross-team acceptance matrix (CSV) listing owners, sign-off dates, and conditional blockers exists and is stored in the PRD folder
Release gate checklist completed: canary plan, metrics to monitor (errors, latency, token cost delta), and rollback criteria documented
updates: 2026-03-03: Kickoff sync held with ENG, DESIGN, and LEGAL. Agreed on single acceptance matrix file ownership (PM). Action: ENG to provide test plan by 2026-03-09
2026-03-05: DESIGN submitted v2 mock for the toggle + migration modal (Drive link). PM requested copy edits for clarity on rollback language

2026-03-09: ENG posted initial migration-runbook draft in GitHub gist; flagged complex KV-cache warmup behavior when toggling mid-session — mitigation proposed (graceful respawn and prefix-compatibility layer)
2026-03-10: LEGAL replied with two redlines to the Terms addendum around cross-border key export; asked for engineering notes on KMS key residency to finalize
2026-03-11: PM consolidated sign-off matrix draft and shared with stakeholders. Next: finalize legal wording and schedule final sign-off meeting 2026-03-15
